text.title: GraphQL API Design Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules grounding the graphql-api-design methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale; the final rule is the skip-this-methodology gate referenced by the decision tree.

rule.statement: Edit the SDL before resolver code; the SDL diff is what humans review.
rule.rationale: Schema-first aligns frontend/backend on a stable contract; resolvers are derived from the schema, not the other way around.

rule.statement: Every resolver that accesses a related entity uses a DataLoader, instantiated per-request in GraphQL context.
rule.rationale: Module-global DataLoaders cache across requests and leak user data; without DataLoader, N+1 queries pass unit tests but destroy prod performance.

rule.statement: Every list field uses Relay-style cursor pagination (first/after, edges, pageInfo). Offset pagination is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Offset pagination produces duplicates (inserts) and gaps (deletes) under concurrent writes; cursors are stable.

rule.statement: Apply QueryDepthLimiter (max 8-10) and QueryComplexityExtension (max 100-500) on every public schema.
rule.rationale: Without limits, a single deeply nested query can drain the DB connection pool and act as a DoS vector.

rule.statement: Every Query and Mutation field touching auth-scoped data declares permission_classes or an equivalent directive. Auth checks in business logic are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Auth checks scattered in business logic are forgotten on new fields; a per-resolver gate catches missing auth before merge.

rule.statement: Every mutation returns a typed <MutationName>Payload carrying the result entity plus a union of typed error types; errors[] is reserved for unexpected failures. Scalar returns (Boolean, ID) from a mutation are forbidden.

rationale.source: GraphQL best practices + Shopify + GitHub schema design

rule.rationale: Union types make expected failures explicit and force clients to handle them; untyped errors[] signals a bug, not a business rule. A payload type also lets you add fields later, which a scalar return can never do without breaking every client.

rule.statement: Validation and business-rule failures are reported in a userErrors array on the payload; only system failures raise GraphQL errors. UserError carries at least field + message, plus an optional machine-readable code.
rule.rationale: Mixing expected user errors into the transport-level errors[] forces every client to write two parallel error paths; one array with one shape collapses them into one.

rule.statement: Authorization is declared in the SDL — a directive such as @auth(scope: ADMIN) on fields and mutations, or an equivalent per-resolver permission class. Resolvers never inline ad-hoc authorization checks.

rationale.source: GraphQL community + Strawberry docs + practitioner experience

rule.rationale: Inline checks drift across resolvers and are silently omitted on new fields; a declared policy is auditable from the schema alone and a coverage report can prove it.

rule.statement: Paginated lists return <Type>Connection { edges { node, cursor }, pageInfo }; mutation arguments are <MutationName>Input; mutation results are <MutationName>Payload. No deviations anywhere in the schema.
rule.rationale: Predictable naming is what lets client codegen and downstream tooling work without a per-schema patch; a single deviation forces every consumer to special-case it.

rule.statement: Relations expose id: ID! as a Relay opaque global ID (gid://app/Type/123), never a raw integer or database UUID. The server decodes; storage detail stays server-side.
rule.rationale: Raw scalars leak the storage layer into the contract, so a later migration from int to UUID becomes a breaking schema change for every client.

rule.statement: When the Applies-If preconditions hold and no Skip-If trigger fires, walk content/04-procedure.xml end-to-end and run the validator before declaring the design done.

rationale.source: F-066 v3 B5.6 — mandatory run leaf

rule.rationale: Decision-tree leaves must reference a rule id; the run leaf maps "all gates green" onto the canonical execution path instead of an unnamed verdict.

rule.statement: If the API is a cacheable public read API OR single-client CRUD OR file-upload-heavy OR the schema is a thin facade over one resource with a single flat auth flag, skip this methodology.
rule.rationale: GraphQL overhead (DataLoader, depth/complexity, persisted queries, directive-based auth) is not paid back outside multi-client, multi-aggregate, nested-read use cases.
